title: Slice restriction and the normalized local derived-Hom comparison
statement:
Let $W$ be a w-contractible affine scheme [sk-def-pe-wlocal], let $S=\pi_0(W)$ with its profinite quotient topology, and let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. Use the small pro-etale site and compatible coefficient universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Give $\operatorname{Prof}/S$ finite jointly surjective coverings, let $q_S$ be its slice projection to the condensed topos, put $\Lambda_S=q_S^*\Lambda$, and let $\pi_W$ be the component morphism with $p_W=q_S\pi_W$ [lem-zl-component-relative-profinite-site]. Write $F_W=\pi_W^*$ on module sheaves and on their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with coefficient identification $F_W\Lambda_S=p_W^*\Lambda$. For each w-contractible affine $U\to W$ put $T=\pi_0(U)$, let $r_U$ be restriction to $W_{\mathrm{proet}}/U\simeq U_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and let $r_T$ be restriction to $\operatorname{Prof}/T$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site, lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Let $F_U=\pi_U^*$ for the component morphism of $U$. There is a canonical natural isomorphism of exact functors on module sheaves, and of the induced unbounded derived functors,
$$r_UF_W\xrightarrow{\sim}F_Ur_T.$$
It identifies the coefficient rings, tensor comparisons, units and pulled-back evaluation maps. For $K,L\in D(\operatorname{Prof}/S,\Lambda_S)$ let $H=R\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_S}(K,L)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and let $\alpha_{K,L}:F_WH\to R\mathcal Hom_{p_W^*\Lambda}(F_WK,F_WL)$ be the transpose of pulled-back tensor-Hom evaluation. Under the derived evaluation comparison [lem-sfb-component-pullback-unbounded-evaluation] and canonical slice restriction of derived internal Hom, the derived-sections morphism $R\Gamma(U,\alpha_{K,L})$ is identified with the evaluation-adjoint morphism
$$R\Gamma(T,R\mathcal Hom(K|_T,L|_T))\longrightarrow R\Gamma(U,R\mathcal Hom(F_U(K|_T),F_U(L|_T))).$$
For every integer $n$, its map on $H^n$, under the canonical derived-Hom sections identifications, is exactly
$$\operatorname{Hom}(K|_T,L|_T[n])\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(F_U(K|_T),F_U(L|_T)[n]),\quad f\longmapsto F_U(f).$$
Consequently if $F_U$ is fully faithful on the unbounded derived categories then $R\Gamma(U,\alpha_{K,L})$ is an isomorphism of derived objects. These comparisons are natural in $K,L$ and compatible with successive restrictions. No boundedness, perfectness or dualizability is assumed.

proof.text: Apply component_pullback_unbounded_evaluation to W and package its continuity, braided structure, exactness, coefficient isomorphism, factorization, and evaluation as PullbackData dW. For each affine w-contractible U apply the same theorem to obtain dU. This is direct record assembly, without choosing a new inverse image.

Apply the ordinary component-slice lemma to the two fixed evaluation data to obtain r and e, monoidal for exactly schemeCanonicalMonoidal. Apply the derived normalization lemma to those same r and e and the monoidality proof. These supply the ordinary and derived clauses in the theorem.

Prove uniqueness directly. For a basis test V and any input section y, choose x by the inverse of basisSections after restrictionSections. The two OrdinaryBasisFormula equations have the same right side, hence give equal values at y. The weakly contractible basis covers each test. Transport the affine and w-contractible conditions along each spectrum isomorphism, restrict both sheaf morphisms to this covering, and use naturality and the basis equality. The sheaf condition makes them equal globally. Faithfulness of the module and sheaf forgetful functors, natural-transformation extensionality and Iso.ext give equality of the ordinary isomorphisms. This also fixes comparisons on every further slice test.

It is a first split of a statement-only node that Q68 created on 2026-10-22, so the re-split rule does not apply. The statement and metadata are unchanged, there are no new nodes, and no SGA is cited. Source: HRS Prop. 4.3(1), PDF p. 8-9. Its proof ends with 'preservation of inner homomorphisms is immediate from full faithfulness using (4.2)', and the item expands exactly that sentence. Full faithfulness of π_U is a hypothesis of the item, so there is no cycle with the parent. Stacks 08JA (sites-cohomology.tex l.8874) and 08JB (l.8934) were checked. Steps: (1) Exactness follows from lem-zl-component-relative-profinite-site, trf inverse-image exactness and pur restriction exactness, and the termwise derived functor with its shift comparison from pbc derived-factorization. (2) c is built on the w-contractible basis by applying the unbounded-evaluation node with base W and again with base U; both identifications give M(P→T→S), and the extension to all objects is written out by gluing over the 098F-type basis. (3) Tensor and unit compatibility comes from the pure-tensor formula of sfb localized-site-tensor-restriction and K-flat preservation in pbc derived-tensor-pullback; D(c) comes from sfb exact-derived-natural-iso. (4) Both equations of lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-evaluation-transpose, applied on Prof/S and on W_proet, together with the closed-monoidal bijection, transport α to β as an equality of morphisms. (5) The pullback-normalized evaluation is used at U→W and at U itself. (6) The sections model gives H^n = Hom(A,B[n]) in every degree, and the explicit uncurrying computation gives f ↦ F_U(f). (7) A K-injective target and a chain-map representative make it a quasi-isomorphism, with no boundedness used. (8) Naturality and successive restrictions follow. Edge cases (U or W empty, U = W, all n, zero inputs) hold. Duplicate search over the dag found no node stating this comparison; lift-lisse-section-comparison, pushforward-exact-unit, zl scalar evaluation and clopen naturality are different statements. Batch-5 flag: lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact is the generic Stacks 04JC fact that inverse image along a geometric morphism is exact, with only generic site/topos proof_deps. It is not given by the trace-formula or Poincaré-duality assumptions and is not a step of their substance; the landed parent already cites it in step 1. Accepted. The declared tool_uses are generic black-box ringed-site and derived-category tools, all accepted.
